$comment: Shared contract between the editor's C# checker and the browser checker (pdf.js). Authoritative copy: testdata/redaction-corpus/redaction-check-spec.json in the abyo PDF Editor repository; the browser checker mirrors it. Both implementations load THIS file for thresholds; neither hard-codes a number. Changing any value or rule bumps specVersion. Version 1 agreed 2026-10-20; version 1.1 agreed 2026-10-20 after the browser checker found false passes (see changes and requirements); version 1.2 agreed 2026-10-20 (annotation flags, word-boundary visible text, A7 recovered words, noteKey earlier-revision-not-read, detail as a code, declared evidence values, dictionary-drawn annotations; #115-#122); version 1.3 agreed 2026-10-20 (closed subpaths measured separately, strokes as per-segment ribbons, A3 takes any dark cover of an annotation, a clip kept as its pieces, every emitted code reached; #123-#134); version 1.4 agreed 2026-10-20 (winding-aware holes, the A3 ladder's two thresholds, coverage against the union of the covers, clip pieces as regions, limits that never reduce what is reported, form values read rather than counted, and the unit of findings outside the contract, the recovered span; #135-#146); version 1.5 opened 2026-10-20 (fixtures found by mutation testing, A9 tooltips, link targets, annotation authors, rich text and subjects, the Off rule for buttons only, remedy text with every new report, clip pieces as regions a MUST, unknown glyphs stay covered, inline image decoding; #147-#158); version 1.6 opened 2026-10-20 (clip visibility as a fraction of the glyph box against the union of the clip pieces, the clip's real region with no hull, A9 signature details and XFA forms, inline filter chains; #150 rewritten, #159-#170; then Codex v107 rounds 3-4 with the browser checker's #171-#194: strokes built in user space with caps and joins, stencil masks in A6, an image cover's parallelogram, sampling without a comb, the cell rule for an image's dark areas, the inks a glyph paints by its mode, the text state across a form, A8 judging every occurrence, and the general rule that a limit floors at review; then Codex v107 round 5 and #195-#225: painted regions for backgrounds, text clip modes, the inks' alpha and the A4/A5 division, dash patterns, stencils in A6, self-crossing subpaths); version 1.7 opened 2026-10-20 (the fill rule by band with nesting and tangles sampled at every vertex and edge midpoint, holes as polygons, weak covers for soft masks and self-crossing fills, background composition with a replacing alpha of 0.999, blends on luminance where the colours allow it and blend classes, the inks of a glyph laid one over the other and a wide stroke swallowing the fill, graded image alpha, curve extent by the control points, dashes and zero-length segments, NoRotate at both placements, the union policy, advances the file does not supply, encryption read from the trailer, zero-area glyph boxes; #226-#278, editor fixtures #279-#280). See docs/design/disclosure-redaction/design.md sections 4.2.1 and 8.

1.7: manifest contract (agreed with the browser checker): the canonical verdict is what a fully capable implementation answers. acceptVerdicts may include pass ONLY when pass is the canonical verdict - a cautious fallback may be accepted beneath a pass, but no case may green-light pass beneath a stricter verdict. expect.checks binds every report whose verdict is not pass (a pass carries no findings), so a canonical pass may - and should - name the checks its cautious fallback must raise: a fallback that is unsure for an unrelated reason does not satisfy the case. #195 #233 (A4) and #242 #259 #268 #271 (A1) are written this way: documents that are fine where they sit, with review on the named check as the fallback for an implementation that cannot establish it

fill rule by band (#239-#265, #275): what each loop of a fill or clip paints is the fill rule's answer at ONE point of its BAND - the part of the loop no loop nested inside it covers - counting the winding of every subpath of the path AS WRITTEN at that point. Never the depth of the loop in a nesting tree, never the signs of its ancestors: three nested rectangles under f* paint the island (winding 3, #255), +,-,+ under f paint the innermost (winding 1, #257).

nesting and tangles (#265, #275, #262): a subpath is NESTED in another only when the point-in-polygon test holds at every vertex AND at the midpoint of every edge of it, and no edge of the one properly crosses an edge of the other. Corners alone fail: a concave shape can hold all of a bar's corners and none of its middle (#265), and a bar whose crossings with a U's notch are written as its own vertices touches without crossing (#275). Two subpaths whose interiors meet - tested at the same points, every vertex and every edge midpoint of each (this engine also measures their common area exactly by triangles) - without one being inside the other form a TANGLE however the path is written: each is emitted as an over-approximated BOUND, painted throughout and marked, the cover's safe direction; a background, a clip or a picture that relies on it floors at review (#262). A loop whose band offers no point to ask the rule at is a bound too.

holes are polygons, never boxes (#254, #256, #257): a hole is taken out as its own outline. Rectangularity (candidate.rectangularity) is the closed subpath's own, a hole not being part of it: a strip cut beside a diamond hole is no reason to drop the rectangle (#254).

self-crossing outlines (#239, #240, #253): a subpath that crosses itself, or returns to one of its own vertices (a crossing written as a named vertex, #253), or rests a vertex inside another of its edges, is split there into loops. Splitting may leave loops that overlap each other (a pentagram): they are tangled, a bound under a rule that leaves the overlap out.

candidate.weakCover (#236, #239, #240, #253): a paint that would be a cover but for what this contract cannot measure - a soft mask (how much it lets through is per pixel), or a fill whose subpath crosses itself and is not rectangular enough (rectangularity cannot rule a self-crossing outline out) - stays in the cover lists as a WEAK cover: text under it with coveredFraction >= coverFail is A1 review (text-under-weak-cover), invisible text under it A5 review (invisible-text-under-weak-cover). Never fail, never dropped. /SMask /None is no mask (#235).

background composition (A4, #258, #263, #264, #269, #278): the background of a glyph is what the paints drawn before it COMPOSE to at its centre, each laid over what is behind it under its own alpha and blend mode: result = (1 - alpha) x backdrop + alpha x B(paint, backdrop). Every paint that paints anything is composed, whatever its alpha - a black band at /ca 0.9 leaves the page a tenth of the way to white (#263); a white Multiply rectangle over a black band leaves it black (#258); a black image under Screen on white paper leaves it white (#264). An image's pixel colour and its alpha stay apart until they are composed: flattening a half-transparent image over paper inside the sampler makes it mid-grey, which then replaced a black band (#278). A paint REPLACES what is under it, known or not, only when its alpha is >= 0.999, its blend mode is Normal or Compatible, and it has no soft mask (#269); at alpha 0.95 the background still shows through and an unknown one stays unknown. A soft-masked paint under the glyph, or a blend that does not compose on luminance for its colours, leaves the background not composed: A4 review (background-not-composed, noteKey fill-colour-unreadable).

blend on luminance (#233): luminance blends exactly only where the colours allow it - Normal and Compatible always (they are linear); Multiply and Screen when either colour is a grey (R = G = B, C = M = Y); Darken and Lighten when both are. Otherwise the ink, or the background, is not read: review, never a confident fail (cyan text Multiplied over red is black on red, readable; its luminances multiply to 0.045). A blend mode is the PDF name - of a /BM array the first recognised, an unrecognised name Normal - never a renderer's own name (#251, pdf.js source-over).

blend classes (candidate.opaque.darkOnlyBlendModes, lightOnlyBlendModes): Normal and Compatible replace: a dark paint is a cover, an opaque light one nonDarkOpaqueCover (review). Multiply and Darken keep the darker, so they hide only by being dark - a pale Multiply box in page content is no cover and gives no A1 review (the #96 neighbourhood). Screen and Lighten mirror them: they keep the lighter, so a dark one hides nothing (#259) and a light one (luminance >= 1 - candidate.dark.maxLuminance) is a non-dark cover (review).

the inks of a glyph (A4, #249, #267, #277): fill and stroke are laid one over the other where they overlap - fill, then stroke - so two faint inks that each stay under hiddenContrast can show together (#249: 1 - 0.9 x 0.9 = 0.19). A mode that fills then strokes (Tr 2, 6) with a pen at least as wide ACROSS THE STEMS as the glyph box is tall swallows the fill: only the stroke reaches the page (#267). The width is the pen's in user space carried by the CTM alone, w x |L^T u| along the direction u the glyph box's height runs - the text matrix does not widen the stroke across the stems it outlines, and the matrix's largest stretch would call a 5 pt pen 50 pt (#277). Whether the stroke swallows the fill is decided by what the render MODE paints, whether or not the stroke's colour is read.

graded image alpha (#268, #278): an image's /SMask is a per-pixel alpha, never transparent-or-solid at a halfway mark. A constant soft mask is a constant alpha composed like /ca (a constant /SMask of 128 is half-transparent: no blackout, #268). An implementation that reads a varying soft mask may compose it pixel by pixel; one that does not keeps the paint as a weak cover and the background not composed.

curve extent (#234, #270): a curve is flattened to a tolerance ON THE PAGE (this engine: 0.1 pt by Wang's bound), measured against the largest stretch of the matrix (its greatest singular value), never a fixed step count nor the square root of its determinant. A Bezier lies inside the convex hull of its control points, which bounds it exactly: wherever flattening is capped or approximate, the paint's extent includes the control points (here an over-approximated region of the paint, grown by the half line width for a stroke). An extent grown by an error estimate is not enough: a curve with control points hundreds of thousands of units away peaks a hundred points beyond every sampled chord (#270).

dashes and zero-length segments (#231, #243, #244, #248, #252, #260, #266, #276): a dash that merely starts at a vertex has a cap, not a join (#231, #243); a dash running through a vertex has a join and no caps (#244); a dash with length still to run carries into the next segment, and where an open path stops it ends with its cap (#248). On a closed path the dash arriving at the start runs into the piece that left it - one piece, a join, no caps - only if there was ink there to run into (#252, #260). A zero-length dash the pattern reaches exactly at the end of a path paints a dot (#266). A zero-length segment as drawn (m then l to the same point, not a lone moveto) is a dot under round caps and a square of the pen's width under projecting caps (#276; 1.6 read ISO 32000-1 8.5.3.2 as round caps only).

NoRotate (#245): viewers disagree where a NoRotate annotation on a turned page lands - PDFium keeps it upright about its /Rect's upper-left corner, pdf.js turns it with the page at /Rect. drawOrder.annotationFlags asks whether an annotation covers text in any view, so it is measured at both placements.

unresolvable appearance states (#246): an /AP /N state dictionary whose selection cannot be resolved is reported, never ignored; each implementation chooses its own state order (this engine: PDFium's /AS, /V, the parent's /V, /Off, else content-truncated appearance-state-not-determined).

union policy (#226, #261): coverage against the union of the covers is computed exactly for up to a bound (this engine: 512 disjoint pieces under one glyph) or REFUSED - review (A1 cover-union-not-measured, content-truncated cover-union-too-complex). Never a summed fraction, never a cell estimate for shapes that are not axis-aligned: both count an overlap twice (the same diamond drawn twice over a seventh of a glyph is a seventh, #261). A hole belongs to the cover that has it (#226). A cover with no pixels subtracts nothing (#247).

advances the file does not supply (#271, #272; Codex v107 round 8): a cover decision that depends on glyph advances the file does not supply - neither an embedded font, nor /Widths, nor one of the standard fourteen - floors at review (this engine: a run of such glyphs whose reach, its first origin to one em per glyph, meets any cover is A1 review cover-decision-on-estimated-advances). The standard fourteen are NOT estimates: their AFM metrics decide, and nothing floors on them. A definite finding the estimate gives stands beside the review.

encryption (#273, #274; Codex v107 round 8): whether a file is encrypted is read from its trailer, /Encrypt as an indirect reference or a direct dictionary alike, never only from an open that fails. An encrypted file whose content could not be decrypted is not examined (A11 review, encrypted-not-decrypted), never passed. An encrypted file that opens but whose pages hold nothing at all floors at review (A11 encrypted-pages-empty): a blank page and a failed decryption cannot be told apart.

zero-area glyph boxes (Codex v107 round 8): a glyph whose advance Tc cancels still draws ink; its box has no area and is judged by its centre everywhere - covered when its centre is hidden (under a stencil as under a rectangle), outside the CropBox or clipped out when its centre is.

peer readings with no change here: a soft-masked paint stays in a cover list (weak cover, above); collinear vertices never invert a clip (#237, this engine orients by signed area); convex means winding once (#238, a pentagram is split at its crossings); a bound outline trimmed away by its own extent proves nothing (an over-approximated painted area that does not contain a point is never read as covering it, and zero coverage from a bound is not used to rule a cover out); A4 refuses a soft-masked background (review, above).

implementation notes (not normative): this engine checks its paints against the browser checker's suite invariant on every corpus walk - a region over-stated where it is painted says so, a blend mode is a PDF name, what a paint paints lies inside its own regions, every region and painted piece has area (RedactionCorpusPaintInvariantTests). Editor fixtures #279 (an Indexed Lab picture, lookup bytes over L* 0..100) and #280 (a Type 3 d0 glyph painting in its own colour) are offered to the browser checker.

manifest readings the editor wrote differently from the browser checker's copy, for the checker to confirm: #234 fail with review accepted (the 0.2 pen under 1000 0 0 100 is 200 pt wide on the page and lays black over intact picture - PDFium's render shows it); #277 review with A4 (23 of its glyphs lie wholly outside the CropBox at a tenfold text matrix); #245 lists A3 (checksSemantics.annotationCovers); #233 #242 #259 #268 #271 written as pass with review accepted (acceptVerdicts may not add pass).
1.6: clip visibility (A4 outside-clip): judged glyph by glyph, never per run. A glyph is drawn under a clip only when the fraction of its glyph box (glyphBox) inside the UNION of the clip pieces is >= coverPartialMin (checks.A2, 0.15); below that it is clipped out. This replaces 1.3's 'outside when its box meets none of the pieces': a box whose edge only touches a piece (#165) or that reaches a point into one (#166) has nothing drawn and was taken as visible. A clip that trims only the descent band leaves four fifths of the box and is not reported (#168, the guard against a threshold set too high); a clip that leaves a tenth is (#169). Per run - one box for the run, or the run visible when any of its glyphs is - calls a clipped name visible because the words beside it are: a false clean

clip union (MUST): the fraction is taken against the union of the pieces, never their summed area. Pieces may overlap (two subpaths of one clip, the strips of a ring), and a sum counts the overlap twice: two thin bands overlapping by nine tenths leave an eighth of each box showing while their sum is a fifth (#170). A capped sum over-states what shows only when pieces overlap, but then it does. An implementation that bounds the union computation, for example by piece count, must on exceeding the bound either compute exactly or floor the page at review. Falling back to a summed area is not conforming, because it can only over-state what shows

clip pieces are the clip's real region: each use of a path's regions errs in its own safe direction. For a cover, the hull of a concave subpath and overlapping subpaths taken as painted throughout over-state the cover, which can only add a finding (candidate.rectangularity, 1.3). For glyph visibility the same over-statement calls a glyph drawn that is not: the pieces MUST be the region the clip path encloses - a concave subpath decomposed into convex pieces (an L-shaped clip with the name in its notch, #160; its arms are the guards, #161 and #162), holes cut out, and an overlap the fill rule leaves unpainted (W*, or nonzero with opposite windings) left out. Where an implementation can only over-estimate the region, a glyph the over-estimate calls visible floors the page at review instead of passing (this engine: A4 finding detail clip-visibility-not-measured, checksSkipped content-truncated with detail clip-too-complex); what an over-estimate clips out is clipped out

A9 signatureDetails: the non-empty /Name, /Reason, /Location and /ContactInfo of every signature dictionary (/Type /Sig, and the /V of a signature field, where /Type is optional) count, each as Key=value. They name and locate a person and travel with the file whether or not a viewer shows them. The certificate inside /Contents names the signer too and is OPTIONAL to read (#159)

A9 xfaForm: an /XFA entry in /AcroForm counts by its PRESENCE (count 1); the packet is not parsed. An XFA form is a second form definition whose data can hold everything somebody typed. Its remedy names the removal that deletes it (#159)

A9 linkTargets and bookmarks (no change, confirmed on #159): a bookmark's URI action and the document's /OpenAction are URI actions like a link's and are read (linkTargets, 1.5); a bookmark's title is listed under bookmarks

imageDecoding (inline images): every filter of an inline image's /F array comes off in order; ASCII85 then Flate is a chain like any other (#163). An inline image behind a filter nothing can decode is a review (image-pixels-not-readable) or, read from its raw bytes, whatever they say; never a pass (#164, acceptVerdicts fail and review)

#150 rewritten: its name is short and sits well inside the triangle's bounding box, so a box in place of the piece passes it and only the region reports it. The first version ran a long line past the box's right edge, and an implementation testing glyph by glyph raised A4 for the glyphs beyond the edge whichever it used

Codex v107 round 3 (rules already stated, read as written): A6 takes every dark candidate, an annotation appearance's included (candidate.sources lists annotationAppearance; A3 asks only about text, so a black /Square over an intact photo must be A6), and samples the image pixels inside the INTERSECTION of the candidate's effective region with the image's effective (clipped) placement, mapped through the image's inverse transform - never a bounding rectangle, which takes in pixels a rotated box does not cover (a correctly redacted picture under a box turned 30 degrees passes) and pixels a clipped picture does not show (a box beside a triangle-clipped picture is no A6). candidate.image 'over the area where' is local: text under the dark area of an image that is not dark as a whole (a black band burned into a light scan) is covered by a dark candidate for A5 and A1 - in this implementation a glyph at least coverFail of whose glyph box lies on strips (along and across the line, 20 each) in which at least minDarkPixelFraction of the samples are dark; coverFail rather than coverPartialMin so that white letters reversed out of a scanned black heading are not a blackout. imageDecoding: an image whose colour space gives some colour no luminance (a Type 4 tint transform with no other decoder, an Indexed table shorter than hival reaches) is an image whose pixels cannot be read - review with image-pixels-not-readable, never a picture that is not there

Codex v107 round 4 - candidate.strokedPath (#180-#182): a stroke's region is built in USER space, where the pen is round: for each segment a ribbon of half the line width either side of it; at each open end a cap as J says (0 butt: none, it stops at the endpoint; 1 round: a disc of the half width; 2 projecting square: the ribbon extended by the half width); at each corner a join as j and M say (0 miter: the wedge out to the miter point while 1/sin(phi/2) <= M, phi the angle between the segments, else bevel; 1 round: a disc; 2 bevel: the triangle between the two outer corners); a degenerate subpath is painted only with round caps, as a dot (ISO 32000-1 8.5.3.2). Each piece is then transformed by the CTM. minLineWidthPt is compared with the width ON THE PAGE across the segment the piece belongs to, |det CTM| * w / |CTM * direction|, never sqrt(|det CTM|) * w, which under 0.1 0 0 10 made a 40 pt horizontal stroke 4 pt and under 1 0 0 0.1 made a 3 pt rule a 9.5 pt cover. A dash pattern is not followed: its gaps are taken as painted (over-states a cover)

Codex v107 round 4 - A6 and stencil masks: an /ImageMask (a 1-bit stencil, often text drawn as an image) is an image for A6. Its samples carry no colour - it paints the fill colour in force where /Decode says (sample 0 under [0 1], 1 under [1 0]) - so darkness is not the question: a black stencil under a black box is invisible and still in the file. Rule: of the samples inside the intersection of the candidate's region with the stencil's placement, the stencil's shape is INTACT when it paints at least one and fewer than candidate.image.minDarkPixelFraction of them -> A6 fail. Painting none (its bits there cleared) or at least minDarkPixelFraction (overwritten solid, the analogue of pixels already blackened, and what a redaction that cannot cut a stencil writes) is no finding. A stencil whose samples cannot be decoded (CCITT, JBIG2 where the implementation does not read them) is review with image-pixels-not-readable, as an image is. A4 likewise takes a stencil as its fill colour only where it paints: in a hole of its shape the background is what lies under it

Codex v107 round 4 - A5 (#191): invisible text with coveredFraction >= coverPartialMin under an image whose pixels cannot be read is a review in EITHER draw order (detail invisible-text-under-undecodable-image, checksSkipped image-pixels-not-readable with the filter); under a cover of unread colour (requirements.shading) it is a review (detail invisible-text-under-cover-of-unread-colour, noteKey fill-colour-unreadable). Before, A5 asked about dark covers only and an OCR layer drawn after an undecodable scan passed

Codex v107 round 4 - drawOrder, the text state across a form (#192): a Form XObject is parsed with a text state of its own, as PDFium's AddForm does: the form starts from the caller's font, size, Tc, Tw and Tr and from the INITIAL text matrix, leading, rise and horizontal scaling, and nothing it does to any of them comes back to the caller. A form shown inside the caller's BT therefore leaves the caller's Tm and Tlm where they were; the caller's next Tj is placed by them. An annotation appearance and a Type 3 glyph procedure likewise start from the initial text matrix

Codex v107 round 4 - A8: every occurrence of a replacement text is judged, THEN the occurrences of one string (page, key, text, source) are reduced to the worst; one finding per string, at its first failing occurrence. De-duplicating first by a key without the region kept the first occurrence (printed in the clear) and dropped the later one under the cover

Codex v107 round 4 - A4, the inks a glyph paints (#189, #190): the inks are its fill for modes 0, 2, 4 and 6 and its stroke for 1, 2, 5 and 6 (none for 3 and 7, which are A5's). A glyph is the same as its background only when EVERY ink it paints is (|L(ink) - L(background)| < hiddenContrast for each): white letters outlined in black on white paper are readable, a white stroke-only line on white paper is not, whatever its unused fill colour. A glyph one of whose inks is of a colour the implementation does not read (a pattern, a tint transform it does not run), and none of whose read inks stands out, is a review (detail text-colour-not-read, noteKey fill-colour-unreadable), never a silent pass. OPEN, for the owner: a BACKGROUND of unread colour (text over a shading) is not judged - spec 1.1 kept a gradient behind text as hiding nothing

Codex v107 round 4 - A4.imageBackground (#187, #188), restated: when the topmost opaque painter under the glyph centre is an image, the background is the measured mean luminance of its pixels under the glyph box, never paper white and never the dark threshold: white letters reversed out of a scanned black band are not A4, black letters on it are

candidate.image region (#183): an image's region is the parallelogram its matrix maps the unit square to, intersected with the clip - never that parallelogram's bounding box, which for an image turned 45 degrees is twice the cover

imageSampling (#185): the samples over a region are one per cell of a 64 x 64 grid over its bounding box, each at a FIXED low-discrepancy offset inside its cell - the Halton point of the cell's index k = row * 64 + column + 1 (van der Corput radical inverse in base 2 across, base 3 down) - never the cell's midpoint. A grid of midpoints is a comb: an image striped with its period (every third of 192 columns black under 64 samples) read fully dark while two thirds of the picture were intact. The offsets are fixed, so a reading is repeatable

candidate.image.cells, the rule for an image's dark areas under text, stated explicitly (#172, #178, #186): the glyph box is divided into 20 x 20 cells along and across the line, each sampled at 3 x 3 fixed low-discrepancy offsets; all 400 cells are in the denominator; a cell is dark when at least minDarkPixelFraction (0.95) of its samples that lie on the image and inside its effective region are dark, and at least one does - a cell off the image is not dark; a sample whose pixel cannot be read counts as dark; the glyph is covered by the image's dark area when at least coverFail (0.85) of its cells are dark (A1 for text drawn before the image, A5 for invisible text in either order). Replaces the 1.6 draft's strips along and across the line

requirements.limits, the general rule (agreed in round 4): a check that examined only part of what it is defined over, because of an implementation limit of ANY kind (entries, pieces, revisions, pages, operators, bytes), reports what it did not reach - a declared skip code with detail - and floors the file at review. A cap never produces a pass. This generalises the Type 3 floor (type3Glyphs.notInspected) and the clip-union floor (A4.clipVisibility). The rule is about SCOPE - something not reached at all - not PRECISION: sampling resolution (a fixed number of samples over a region, the cells over a glyph box) approximates the whole region and does not trigger it, nor does a display cap on recovered text (a quoted length marked with an ellipsis). revisions-not-readable keeps its own, more precise floor (review only when nothing at all could be read, #109) and is left out of the blanket floor on purpose: a revision chain longer than an implementation follows is revisions-not-readable with detail chain. An approximation at a bound must lean the safe way FOR ITS USE, or floor: a union approximated by a sum over-states what a COVER hides (safe for text under it) but over-states what a CLIP shows (a false pass), so the clip floors; a cover region over-stated at a bound (holes left in, nesting not analysed) is safe for text under it, but A6's samples and A4's background inside its holes are pixels and paper it does not hide, so A6 (cover-region-over-stated) and A4 (background-region-over-stated) floor at review (content-truncated path-region-over-stated). In the editor's engine: a structure tree past its walk (A8, content-truncated structure-tree-too-large), a file read from its bytes past its bounds (A8, content-truncated file-bytes-not-fully-read), a ring of more holes than it cuts (the outer taken solid, with the floors above)

fixtures #171-#194 from the browser checker. #171 (thirteen overlapping clip bands) is pass by the exact union and review where a bounded union is exceeded (acceptVerdicts pass and review). #177 keeps acceptVerdicts fail and review (an inline Separation image with a Type 4 tint transform: the browser checker evaluates it, the editor reports it unread). #193 (sixty /ActualText entries in /PieceInfo) names no check: the editor's A8 reads marked content and structure elements only (checks.A8) and reaches /PieceInfo through A9. #194 (an earlier revision of sixty draft lines) is A7 fail: the editor reads every string of a revision

Codex v107 round 5 - A4 background, the region a paint REALLY paints (#205, #206): the background at the glyph centre is the topmost opaque paint drawn before the glyph whose painted region contains the centre - the region the path's fill rule paints, never its hull or bounding box (a concave subpath decomposed, e.g. by ear clipping; the overlap of two subpaths the fill rule leaves unpainted left out; the gaps of a dash pattern left out), cut by the clip's real region (clip pieces, 1.5/1.6). Before, an L drawn as one concave path was its hull, so white text in its notch read as white on black (a pass of white-on-white) and black text there as black on black. Each use of a region errs its own safe direction (requirements.limits): a cover may be over-stated, a background may not - where an implementation knows only an over-statement and the centre lies in it, the glyph is not judged: REVIEW (this engine: A4 detail background-region-over-stated, checksSkipped content-truncated path-region-over-stated). The same holds for A6: the pixels sampled are those the cover really paints and the picture really shows; where either is only over-stated, REVIEW (cover-region-over-stated)

Codex v107 round 5 - text clip modes (#208): glyphs shown in Tr 4, 5, 6 and 7 add their outlines to a text clip; at ET the clip in force is intersected with the union of those outlines for everything drawn after, until the graphics state is restored (ISO 32000-1 9.3.6). An implementation that does not read glyph outlines may take each outline as its glyph box (glyphBox), which over-states it: text the boxes leave out is clipped out (A4 outside-clip, fail near a candidate, else review), text inside them is not proven visible and floors the page at review (this engine: clip-visibility-not-measured). Fail is accepted from an implementation that has the outlines

Codex v107 round 5 - the inks' alpha (#207): each ink of a glyph (fill for 0/2/4/6, stroke for 1/2/5/6) carries its constant alpha (ca for the fill, CA for the stroke, set directly or through an ExtGState). The A4/A5 division (agreed with the browser checker; supersedes round 5's 'alpha below hiddenContrast is A5'): A5 is text that paints NOTHING at all - Tr 3, Tr 7, or every ink it paints at an alpha of exactly 0 - judged exactly like Tr 3 (under a candidate: fail; on paper: no finding). A4 is text whose ink does not stand out from what is behind it, faint ink included: any alpha above 0 is A4's, judged against the background at each glyph (#224: white at /ca 0.1 over a black band is A4 same-as-background, fail; #225 at /ca 0.5 is its guard). Partial alpha (A4): an ink shows when alpha * |B(L(ink), L(bg)) - L(bg)| >= hiddenContrast, B the blend mode applied to the luminances (Normal and Compatible: L(ink); Multiply: their product; Screen: L(ink) + L(bg) - their product; Darken: the lesser; Lighten: the greater); the glyph is the same as its background when no ink shows. An ink under a soft mask that would show unmasked, or composited with any other blend mode, is undecided: REVIEW (text-colour-not-read, noteKey fill-colour-unreadable), never a pass

candidate.strokedPath, dash patterns (#201, supersedes round 4's 'a dash pattern is not followed'): a stroke under a dash pattern (d, or an ExtGState /D) paints its dashes only. Each subpath is cut in user space, from the dash phase afresh, into the open pieces the dashes draw (an odd array repeats with dashes and gaps swapped; a dash carries round a corner; a zero-length dash is a dot with its cap shape - a disc under round caps, a square of the line width along the path under projecting square caps, nothing under butt caps (#221), so [0 5] 0 d with round caps is a dotted rule, never dropped), and each piece is stroked with its caps and joins. Caps belong only to the ENDS of an open subpath and of each dash; an internal vertex is a join, so a stroke that doubles back (200 500 m 220 500 l 200 500 l S) stops at the turn (#223). An odd-length array repeats into its real period, twice its sum, and the phase is taken in that period: [3] 4 d starts one unit into its first gap (#222). An empty array, all zeros or a negative length is solid. An implementation that does not follow the pattern takes the stroke solid and must treat it as over-stated: safe for a cover, REVIEW where a background or A6's pixels rely on it

A6 and stencil masks, the painted area (#210, #213): a stencil candidate hides what is under it only where it paints an area a cover could be (candidate.size): a sample under it counts when the stencil paints at the sample and at the points minShortSidePt / 2 away around it. A speck or the strokes of text drawn as a mask is no cover of the picture under it (#210 pass); a painted band over an intact photograph is A6 fail with no text near it (#213). A stencil whose samples cannot be read cannot rule a sample out: REVIEW (cover-region-over-stated)

self-crossing subpaths (#215): a closed subpath that crosses itself is the simple loops it splits into at its crossings, each with its own winding, and the fill rule is applied to those (a bow-tie is its two lobes). Neither its bounding box (which puts the gaps between the lobes inside it) nor its signed area (which cancels to zero for a bow-tie and calls it empty: as a clip everything is clipped out, as a fill nothing is painted). An implementation that cannot split a subpath takes its hull and marks it as an over-statement (safe for a cover; REVIEW for a background, A6 pixels and clip visibility). Holes are subtracted as the regions they are, never their bounding boxes (#218); coverage is measured against regions and their clips, never bounding rectangles (#219, #220)
stencil masks (#216): a stencil whose every sample paints (a 1 x 1 opaque mask scaled to a block, which pdf.js reports as paintSolidColorImageMask) is a solid cover of its whole parallelogram

implementation note, not normative: an implementation may carry with each region whether it is exact or an over-statement (this engine: RegionFidelity Exact / OverApproximated on PathRegion and PaintedArea). What the spec requires is the limits rule and the safe direction per use: a cover may be over-stated; a background, A6's pixels and clip visibility may not, and where only an over-statement is known they floor at review

fixtures #214-#225 from the browser checker. #214 (a form /BBox clips its text away) and #215 (text in the gap of a bow-tie clip) are review with fail accepted (clipped out away from a candidate). #224 is A4 fail and #225 its guard (the A4/A5 division); #217 (/ca 0.94) passes. #221 is fail for both implementations: the zero-length dashes are dots

fixtures #195-#213 from the browser checker. #195 (pattern-filled text) is written as #171: pass, review accepted (acceptVerdicts may not add pass to a stricter verdict); the editor reports review (text-colour-not-read). #208 is review with fail accepted. #213 is fail for the editor (A6 reads where the stencil paints); the browser checker declares it a gap

Codex v107 round 7 - annotation NoRotate (drawOrder, annotationAppearance): an annotation whose /F has NoRotate (bit 5, value 16) on a page whose /Rotate is 90, 180 or 270 stays upright on screen (ISO 32000-1 12.5.3). Its appearance, placed on /Rect by Algorithm 8.1, is then turned about the upper-left corner of /Rect (min x, max y) by the page's rotation, counter-clockwise in user space (PDFium's AnnotGetMatrix: translate by minus the corner, rotate by rotation x pi/2, translate back); the clip and an appearance synthesized without /AP are turned with it. On /Rotate 90 a NoRotate black /Rect [100 500 300 550] covers x 100..150, y 550..750 and hides text at (110, 650); text under the unturned /Rect is not covered. NoZoom (bit 4) is not followed (PDFium does not; at the reference scale the appearance fills /Rect)

Codex v107 round 7 - appearance states: when /AP /N is a dictionary of states, the state drawn is selected as PDFium selects it (GetAnnotAPInternal): the state /AS names; without /AS, the annotation's /V, else its direct /Parent's /V, when the dictionary has that key; otherwise /Off. The entry selected is drawn when it is a stream; nothing is drawn when it is not. A black /Off state of a square without /AS therefore covers the text under it (A3 fail); it used to be read as no appearance. /AS and /V are read as a name, or as a string naming the state; a value of another type (a number, an array) leaves the state undetermined and floors the page at review (this engine: checksSkipped content-truncated, detail appearance-state-not-determined)

Codex v107 round 7 - stencil masks cover only where they paint (A1, A2, A3, A5, A8, A4 near-candidate): a candidate that is an /ImageMask is opaque and dark by its fill colour, but its effective region for coveredFraction is the set of points of its parallelogram where its samples paint (sample 0 under the default /Decode [0 1], 1 under [1 0]), never the whole parallelogram. An 8 x 8 mask of all ones (paints nothing) over text is no cover (no A1, no A2, no A5), nor is a mask that paints beside the text and not on it; a mask that paints the lower part of each glyph is a partial cover (A2). This engine samples the glyph box at 40 x 40 fixed Halton points and counts a point covered when a polygon candidate's region holds it or a stencil's region holds it and the stencil paints there (an unreadable pixel counts as painted); without a stencil the polygon union is exact as before. A stencil whose samples cannot be decoded (CCITT, JBIG2) is not a dark cover but an undecodable image: review (image-pixels-not-readable), never fail; for A6 it remains a cover of unknown painted area (review cover-region-over-stated)
1.5: clip pieces as regions (MUST, was SHOULD in 1.4): when a clip piece is used for glyph visibility (A4 outside-clip), the piece MUST be the region its subpath encloses, never that subpath's bounding box. The bounding box of a triangle (#150) or of a rectangle turned by a rotation (#153, what a landscape scan placed by a rotation makes) adds corners where nothing is drawn, and text there was taken as drawn: a false pass. #153 discriminates for an implementation that tests glyph by glyph (#150's line also runs past its box, so such an implementation reports it either way). #151 and #154 are the guards (text the clip keeps is not reported)

glyphBox (coverage of an unknown glyph): a glyph never drops out of coverage because its character is unknown or unmappable; only a glyph that maps to white space may be ignored. A font with /Differences glyph names and no /ToUnicode under a black bar is covered text (#158), whatever an extractor makes of the names

imageDecoding (inline images): an inline image's samples are read like an image XObject's, its /Decode (/D) applied. A /Decode [1 0] image of 255s is black and is a dark cover (#155); without /Decode the same samples are white, an opaque cover that is not dark (#156, review)

A9 annotationText and annotationAuthors: an annotation's /RC (rich text) and /Subj count as annotation text whatever the subtype, like /Contents. A markup annotation's /T is its author, a person's name, and counts as its own kind (annotationAuthors); a widget's /T is its field name and is not an author. /Subj is OPTIONAL to list, because pdf.js does not expose it; an implementation that lists it conforms (#152)

A9 formValues (Off): only the NAME /Off on a button field (/FT /Btn, inherited through /Parent) is the unset state and not a value. The STRING (Off), and any value of a field that is not a button, is something somebody typed and counts (#157)
remedy text: when a check learns to report something new, its remedy text is part of the change (verdicts.wordingRules). A9's remedy names every kind it lists, bookmark titles and XMP explicitly

A9 tooltips and linkTargets: two more kinds A9 lists (kind codes tooltips and linkTargets). A form field's /TU always counts; a link's /URI counts only when it is mailto:, carries user information or carries a query string, so a plain web address is not listed. As for every A9 kind, the values are for the screen (recovered) and the saved report keeps the kind and the count

fixtures found by mutation testing: a mutation that leaves every corpus case passing marks arithmetic no file exercises. #147 puts every glyph of a line under two dark bars whose union leaves a band showing (A2, mustNotFlag A1: an exact union that reported everything as fully covered passed every earlier case); #148 draws a black bar under a matrix rotated twelve degrees (the first cover whose transform is neither a translation nor a scale); #149 places a black image by such a matrix, so deciding whether its pixels are dark under a glyph needs the inverse with its cross terms. No rule changes with them: they hold rules already stated (glyphBox.coverage, candidate.rectangularity, the image cover of candidate)
1.4: candidate.region (hole rule, restated): whether a nested subpath is a hole is decided by the fill rule on the actual winding numbers, never by nesting alone. Under even-odd a point is painted when it is enclosed an odd number of times. Under nonzero it is painted when the sum of the windings around it (each subpath's orientation, read from the sign of its area) is not zero: an inner subpath wound against its outer is a hole (#135 under even-odd, guarded by #136 with the text on the band), one wound the same way is not, and the shape is solid (#137). An implementation that treats any nesting as a hole calls text inside a solid shape visible

A3 ladder (reminder): the ladder has two thresholds. A dark appearance fails from coverPartialMin; an appearance that is only opaque is a review only from coverFail. Applying coverPartialMin to every opaque appearance reports an ordinary pale box that merely touches a line. coveredFraction remains per glyph box (coveredFraction(glyphBox, candidate)), so a pale box that hides the first glyphs of a line whole is the middle rung, a review (#138); measuring over the whole line would let a grey box over one name in a sentence pass

glyphBox.coverage: a glyph's coveredFraction is measured against the UNION of all the dark covers drawn after it, not cover by cover (no maximum over single covers, no sum). Two bars meeting on a seam through a glyph cover it fully, an A1 and not a partial cover (A2) by each (#139); ten narrow abutting bars, each covering a tenth of a line, hide all of it (#140). The same holds wherever a check compares coveredFraction with a threshold for dark covers: A1, A2, A5, and the dark covers of one annotation's appearance for A3. Non-dark and unread-colour covers are still measured one at a time

clip pieces as regions: when a clip piece is used for glyph visibility (A4 outside-clip), the piece SHOULD be the region its subpath encloses, not that subpath's bounding box. A bounding box is larger than a rotated or non-rectangular piece, so text in the corner it adds is taken as drawn: a narrow miss, hence SHOULD and not MUST

limits: a cap or limit inside an implementation must never reduce what is reported. Exceeding it either over-states coverage, or marks the page as not fully examined (the reviewFloor, with a declared checksSkipped reason or noteKey). It never falls back to an approximation that can hide text. A clip kept as the hull of its pieces once their number passed a cap made the gaps between the pieces part of the clip, and text in a gap passed with no finding (#144: a name in the gap between two bands of eighty clip pieces, inside their hull)

A9 formValues: a form value is what a terminal field's /V holds, read from the field tree and from widget annotations: a text string (#141), a name, or an ARRAY of strings or names (a multi-select choice, #142). A field that exists without a value, an empty string, and the name Off on a button field (a check box or radio button that is not set; 1.5: the string (Off), or Off on a field that is not a button, IS a value, #157) are not values; counting the fields that exist reports values on a blank form (#143)
findings: the number of findings and their unit (one per cover, per run or per glyph) are NOT part of the contract. What a manifest case states - the verdict, the required checks and mustNotFlag - is

recovered span: the recovered text of a cover finding (A1, A2, A3, A5) is, for each line, the span from the first covered character to the last, read back from the run so that its spaces survive - including a gap written as a move rather than a space glyph: "amada Taro of Yoko", not "amadaTaroofYoko". Never the whole run: the uncovered words around the span are still printed on the page and are not recovered from under anything (#145, #146)

what the manifest constrains: the verdict and which checks fire (expect.checks, mustNotFlag). What a finding says - its recovered text, its evidence - is constrained by each implementation's own tests
1.3: candidate.rectangularity / candidate.region: a filled path is measured one closed subpath at a time. Each subpath is its own painted region with its own rectangularity, so two bars painted by one fill operator are two covers (#123), not one hull about 5% filled. A subpath nested inside another is a hole when the fill rule leaves its inside unpainted (even-odd, or nonzero with the windings cancelling): the outer then covers only the ring around the hole, never the hole. Subpaths that overlap without nesting are each taken as painted throughout (an over-estimate, the safe direction for A1). Subpaths that touch and together are rectangular may be measured as one region, so a glyph on the seam between two abutting bars is not split between them

candidate.strokedPath: a stroke paints a ribbon along each segment of each subpath (the closing segment included for a closed subpath), each the segment grown by half the line width, never the area the path encloses. A frame drawn after text is not a cover of the text inside it (#124), and a frame drawn before text is not the background that text is read against (A4, #125). A fill-and-stroke (B, B*, b, b*) is its fill regions and then its ribbons, so a white box with a black border over text is still an opaque non-dark cover (#126)

A3: every cover an annotation's appearance paints is considered, not the first in draw order. The annotation fails when any dark cover covers text with coveredFraction >= coverPartialMin; otherwise it is a review when a non-dark opaque cover covers text with coveredFraction >= coverFail. Still one finding per annotation (#127)

clip: W and W* mark the path that the NEXT painting operator (n, f, S, ...) ends; that path, not an earlier one, becomes the clip when it is painted (ISO 32000-1 8.5.4). An implementation that applies W to the path before it applies no clip at all (#128)

clip: a clip is kept as its pieces - the regions its closed subpaths enclose under W's fill rule (nonzero for W, even-odd for W*), each measured as candidate.rectangularity measures a fill - intersected piece by piece with the clip in force. A glyph is outside the clip (A4) when its box meets none of the pieces: the hull of two clip rectangles covers the gap between them and would call text in the gap visible (#129); text inside a piece is not reported (#130)

clip: a paint's effective region is the paint intersected with each clip piece, so a bar clipped to half a name covers half of it, an A2 and not an A1 (#131). An implementation may trim covers by the clip's hull instead (an over-estimate of the cover, the safe direction for A1/A2), but MUST test glyph visibility against the pieces

reachability: every finding detail, noteKey and checksSkipped reason an implementation can emit is reached by at least one corpus file or by a named rule test, or is declared unreached with a written reason. #132 (an undecodable image as the cover, A1 checksSkipped image-pixels-not-readable), #133 (a dark bar over an undecodable image, A6) and #134 (#111 with its /Prev broken too) were added because no file reached those branches

A9 documentInfo on a repaired file: when the document opens only through a repair (a broken /Prev), the document information the LAST trailer names is read from the bytes as well; a repair that takes another trailer must not lose it (#134)
1.2: drawOrder.annotationFlags: Hidden (/F bit 2) is not drawn and is not a cover (#116); NoView (bit 6) is still a cover, because it covers on paper; Print (bit 3) clear is still a cover, because it covers on screen; /Redact is A3 whatever its flags

visibleText: one normative visible-text filter for A7 and A8. Words are matched on word boundaries against the visible text with its white space kept (a glyph gap or a line change separates text); a hidden 'Li' is not visible inside a printed 'Click' or 'Lions' (#117). The white-space-insensitive comparison of 1.1 remains only as a fallback for a string of several words broken by a re-flow (#114), never for a single word

A7: words are the letter-or-digit runs of each white-space-separated string; only hidden words are recovered, and a string all of whose words are hidden is recovered as written, so a date stays one string (#115)
A7: outcome 3 (and the chain floor's finding) carries noteKey earlier-revision-not-read
finding.noteKey: earlier-revision-not-read; read-from-file-bytes names A7 as well as A8

finding.detail: a code matching ^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$ (page-not-examined: the failure name), never document text; string evidence values are codes or standard PDF names, and an annotation subtype outside the standard list is written as other. The saved report is byte-identical whether or not findings carry recovered text

finding.detail / finding.evidence: the failure name of a page-not-examined finding (a library's error type name) may be carried in detail or in evidence.failure; both conform, and a comparison of two reports never depends on which

finding.evidence: every string evidence key has declared values, a closed set of codes and standard PDF names or the kind failure name; a value outside its key's declaration, or a string key with no declaration, is non-conformant. checksSkipped detail likewise: an image filter ISO 32000 does not define is written as other, never the document's spelling
visibleText.lineChange: a separation taken from an extractor must survive a line change (#118, a word at the start of a line joined to the line before it)
drawOrder.annotationFlags: a Hidden /Redact is still A3 (#119)

annotationAppearance.withoutAppearance: only Square, Circle and Highlight are drawn from the dictionary; any other subtype with no usable appearance, standard (#122) or unknown (#121), draws nothing and is not a cover. An unknown subtype WITH an appearance is judged by what it paints, like any other (#120)
1.1: requirements: four normative requirements (formXObject, annotationAppearance, shading, strokeState), each with a corpus fixture (#99-#103); an implementation that misses one passes a leaking file
checksSemantics: implementations agree on the VERDICT; expect.checks is a required subset, extra checks are allowed except those in mustNotFlag
A3: the ladder (/Redact or a dark appearance -> fail; opaque but light -> review; a /Highlight that is not dark -> no finding)
A9: which document-information entries count, in PDF terms; annotation /Contents is listed explicitly (#107)

A10: coverage is the SUM of the areas of the page's image paints, each after CTM and clip and intersected with the CropBox, over the CropBox area, capped at 1 (v1: one image). Not their union bounding box: two small images in opposite corners would span the page (#106)
A11: fires only when the file cannot be opened; owner-password-only files are examined and pass A11
glyphBox.vertical: the box for vertical writing mode
units.luminance: annotation colour arrays and Lab
fileReport.notInspected: fixed keys instead of sentences
candidate.sources: shading
type3Glyphs: expanding Type 3 glyph procedures is RECOMMENDED; an implementation that cannot must report type3-glyph-not-inspected and never pass the file (#104)

checksSkipped: reasons are fixed codes (reasonCodes); page, count and detail are separate fields, never interpolated. image-codec-not-decodable:<Filter> became image-pixels-not-readable with detail = the filter
finding.noteKey: a fixed code when a finding says something could not be examined; such a finding is not rendered with the check's generic description and remedy
verdicts.wording.passWithSkipped: the pass headline is qualified whenever checksSkipped is non-empty

checksSkipped: reason check-failed (page, detail = the failure name) for an internal failure while examining a page; the other pages are still examined, and the page carries a review finding with noteKey page-not-examined, so the file is never pass (verdicts.reviewFloor)
finding.noteKey: page-not-examined

A7: earlier revisions are found by the cross-reference chain AND by surplus %%EOF markers (revisionDiscovery, #108, #109); three outcomes (fail / nothing / review), and 'all recovered text is visible' needs something read (#110, #111)
checksSkipped: reason revisions-not-readable for A7, detail chain or revision, with its floor in verdicts.reviewFloor
verdicts.reviewFloor: page-level failures are carried on A1 and mean that none of the page-level checks ran on that page
manifest.sharedExpectations: where shared expectations stop

A7/A8/A9 onOpenFailure: when the file cannot be opened, A7, A8 and A9 run from the file's bytes; A7 and A8 are review there (noteKey read-from-file-bytes); A9 lists document information, attachments and JavaScript; they are in checksRun, not checksSkipped (#112, #113)
finding.noteKey: read-from-file-bytes
A7/A8 visible-text filter: the comparison ignores white space on both sides (#114)

units.length: PDF points in the page's user space after CTM and clipping, before /Rotate; origin bottom-left (rect = x0,y0,x1,y1 with x0<x1, y0<y1)
units.luminance: L = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on 0..1 components as written in the PDF (no gamma decoding). DeviceGray g -> R=G=B=g. DeviceCMYK -> R=(1-C)(1-K), G=(1-M)(1-K), B=(1-Y)(1-K). ICCBased/CalRGB: use the alternate/N-component rule above. Lab: L = L*/100 (a* and b* ignored). Indexed: look up the base; 1.6 (Codex v107 round 6): a lookup byte b is min + b * (max - min) / 255 of its base component's range - 0..1 for the device and Cal spaces, L* 0..100 and a*, b* by /Range (default -100..100) for Lab, the profile's /Range for ICCBased - never b / 255 for every base (a Lab white, byte 255, is L* 100; divided by 255 it was L* 1, dark). An ICCBased colour with a /Range is brought to 0..1 through it before the N-component rule, and a profile whose header names Lab is read lightness first; an image's default /Decode is the same ranges. Separation/DeviceN: tint transform when available, else unknown: never a dark candidate, and a cover of unknown colour is graded like requirements.shading (review, noteKey fill-colour-unreadable). An annotation colour array (/C, /IC) is read by its length (1 gray, 3 RGB, 4 CMYK, 0 = transparent) with every component normalised to 0..1 before the formula (clamped; an implementation whose library returns 0..255 divides by 255 first).

checksSemantics.verdict: Two implementations, and an implementation and the manifest, must agree on the file VERDICT (fail/review/pass).
checksSemantics.checks: expect.checks is a REQUIRED SUBSET: every listed check must be raised; checks not listed may also be raised, except those in expect.mustNotFlag, whose appearance is a false positive.
checksSemantics.annotationCovers: A cover drawn by an annotation appearance must raise A3. An implementation MAY also raise A1 for it (the browser checker does, the editor does not); a manifest lists only A3 for such a cover.
checksSemantics.$comment: Agreed 2026-10-20 (v1.1). Rect and per-finding detail are not part of the contract; a differential run compares verdict, the raised-check set within these rules, and page numbers.

verdicts.fileVerdict: worst finding verdict; pass when there are no findings. A check listed in checksSkipped never yields pass for that check (the one exception is revisions-not-readable with detail chain, see reviewFloor); the report must show it.
verdicts.reviewFloor: A file that was not completely examined is never pass: the verdict is at least review. In particular a page with checksSkipped reason check-failed carries an A1 finding with verdict review, the page, noteKey page-not-examined and detail = the failure name; findings already made on that page and on every other page are kept, and the remaining pages and the document checks are still examined (a file that leaks on page 1 and fails internally on page 3 still reports the page-1 fail). A7: revisions-not-readable with detail revision (an earlier revision exists and nothing legible could be read from it) always floors the verdict at review, with an A7 review finding; detail chain (the cross-reference chain cannot be followed, or a byte prefix found by an %%EOF marker does not open) floors it at review ONLY when nothing at all could be read from the earlier bytes - when another earlier revision was read, the entry is listed and the pass headline is qualified (wording.passWithSkipped), but no finding is added.
verdicts.pageLevelCarrier: page-not-examined and type3-not-inspected findings, and their checksSkipped entries (check-failed, type3-glyph-not-inspected), are carried on A1 by convention. A1 is only the carrier: a page that could not be examined means that NONE of the page-level checks (A1-A6, A10) ran on that page. An implementation MUST NOT list every page-level check for a failed page, and the reader-facing sentence describes the page, not the check.

wording.pass: 検査した{n}項目で問題は見つかりませんでした
wording.passWithSkipped: 検査した{n}項目で問題は見つかりませんでした。ただし、文書の一部で実行できなかった検査があります

wordingRules: When checksSkipped is non-empty, an implementation MUST NOT present the pass headline as 'n checks found nothing' without qualification; it uses passWithSkipped, which states that some checks could not run on part of the document.

A finding that carries a noteKey says the implementation could not examine something; it MUST NOT be rendered with the check's generic description and remedy (which would claim a problem was found) - each surface shows its own sentence for the noteKey.
Neither checksSkipped reasons nor noteKeys are ever shown as raw codes or extended with text; every surface owns the sentence for each code.

When a check learns to report something new, its remedy text is part of the change (1.5): the remedy a finding shows names what the reader is looking at and what removes it, in every shipped language. For A9 that means every kind it lists, including the two the usual advice misses: bookmark titles, which clearing the document information does not touch, and XMP metadata, a store separate from the document properties that many tools leave behind when the properties are cleared. How an implementation checks this is its own (this one declares the words each kind's remedy must contain and fails a build in which a kind it can emit lacks them).

drawOrder.rule: Page content stream(s) in order, with every Form XObject expanded at its Do (recursively, including nested forms, patterns are NOT expanded) under requirements.formXObject, then each annotation's normal appearance (/AP /N, honouring /F under annotationFlags and /OC off) in /Annots order, placed under requirements.annotationAppearance. Annotations are always above page content.
drawOrder.annotationFlags: v1.2. The check asks whether an annotation covers text on screen OR on paper. Hidden (/F bit 2, value 2): drawn nowhere, so it is not a cover and raises no A1, A2 or A3 (#116); Hidden wins over every other flag. NoView (bit 6, value 32): not shown on screen but printed, so it is still a cover - a printed copy shows the box while the text under it can be extracted. Print (bit 3, value 4) clear: shown on screen but not printed, so it is still a cover. Invisible (bit 1) concerns only annotation types a viewer does not know and is not read. A /Redact annotation is reported by A3 whatever its flags (an unapplied redaction mark, regardless of what it draws).

requirements.$comment: Normative since v1.1. Each one is a way an implementation reported a file with readable text under an opaque cover as clean; the fixture named is the case that goes wrong without it.

formXObject.rule: Everything drawn inside a Form XObject is transformed by the form's /Matrix (concatenated onto the CTM at the Do) and clipped by the form's /BBox mapped through that matrix. A cover placed only by the form matrix is a cover where the matrix puts it.
formXObject.textState: 1.6: a form is parsed with a text state of its own (PDFium AddForm): it starts from the caller's font, size, Tc, Tw and Tr and the initial text matrix, leading, rise and horizontal scaling, and nothing it changes comes back to the caller - a form shown inside the caller's BT leaves the caller's Tm and Tlm where they were (#192)

annotationAppearance.rule: An annotation's appearance stream is fitted to /Rect per PDF 32000-1 12.5.5 (Algorithm 8.1): transform the appearance /BBox by its /Matrix, take the bounding box of the result, and map that box onto /Rect (scale and translate); the appearance's content is drawn through /Matrix then that mapping, clipped to /Rect. The colour comes from the appearance stream, not from /C or /IC.
annotationAppearance.withoutAppearance: An annotation with no usable /AP /N is drawn from /IC, else /C (units.luminance for the array): a Square fills its /Rect, a Circle the ellipse inscribed in /Rect, a Highlight its /QuadPoints quads (none -> nothing drawn) with blend mode Multiply; /CA is the alpha. No colour -> nothing drawn. /Redact is A3 regardless of what it draws. v1.2: ONLY these three subtypes are drawn from the dictionary, because only for them does a viewer synthesise an appearance from /IC or /C; an annotation of any other subtype with no usable /AP /N draws nothing and is not a cover, whether its subtype is a standard one (a Stamp with a black /IC, #122) or one ISO 32000 does not define (#121). An annotation of an unknown subtype that HAS an appearance is drawn like any other and judged by what it paints (A3, #120).

shading.rule: A shading - the sh operator, which paints the current clip (the whole page when unclipped), or a fill or stroke whose colour is a pattern (shading or tiling) - is a cover whose colour cannot be read from the content stream. When it is opaque and cover-shaped (candidate.opaque and candidate.size on its effective region) and covers earlier text with coveredFraction >= coverFail, it is an unreadable cover: an A1 finding with verdict below and noteKey fill-colour-unreadable - never fail, never silently ignored. The check did run, so this is a finding, not a checksSkipped entry.

strokeState.rule: Stroke colour (G, RG, K, CS/SC/SCN) and stroke alpha (CA, including CA set through an ExtGState with gs) are tracked separately from the fill colour and fill alpha (g, rg, k, cs/sc/scn, ca). A stroked path is graded by the stroke colour and stroke alpha only; a filled path by the fill state only.

limits.rule: A cap or limit inside an implementation must never reduce what is reported. Exceeding it either over-states coverage, or marks the page as not fully examined (verdicts.reviewFloor, with a declared checksSkipped reason or noteKey). It never falls back to an approximation that can hide text (1.4) 1.6 general rule: a check that examined only part of what it is defined over because of an implementation limit of any kind reports what it did not reach (a declared skip code with detail) and floors the file at review; a cap never produces a pass. It concerns scope, not precision: sampling resolution and a display cap on recovered text do not trigger it; revisions-not-readable keeps its own floor; an approximation at a bound leans the safe way for its use (a cover may be over-stated, a clip may not), or floors.

visibleText.rule: v1.2. Whether a string is shown in the current document (A7's words, A8's replacement texts). The visible text is the extracted text of the page (A8) or of every page (A7) with white space kept, and with a separator between two consecutive glyphs that are not adjacent: on another line, or with a gap along the line wider than wordGapEm times the font size (a word gap written as a TJ adjustment or a move instead of a space). A word is shown when it occurs in the visible text on word boundaries: the character before the match and the character after it are each absent, not a letter or digit, or (with the neighbouring matched character) a CJK ideograph or kana, scripts written without spaces. A word is never shown by the inside of a longer word: a hidden 'Li' is not shown by a printed 'Click' or 'Lions' (#117).
visibleText.multiWord: A string of several words is shown when it occurs, each run of white space matching any run of white space, on word boundaries; failing that, when its characters without white space occur in the visible text without white space, and the match begins and ends on word boundaries of the visible text (a re-flow that split the string across lines or runs, #114). This white-space-insensitive fallback is NEVER used for a single word: a word split by a separator is reported, which is a false alarm at worst, whereas joining words would let a short name hide in a longer one.
visibleText.lineChange: an implementation that takes word separation from its extractor must satisfy itself that the separation survives a line change; consulting both the run-joined and run-separated forms is one way.

type3Glyphs.rule: A Type 3 font's glyphs are drawn by its /CharProcs procedures, which may paint covers. Expanding them is RECOMMENDED: walk the procedure of each shown glyph through /FontMatrix, then the text rendering matrix ([Tfs*Th 0 0 Tfs 0 Trise] x Tm), then the CTM, using the font's /Resources (else the page's). After d1 the glyph is a stencil: its colour operators are ignored and it paints in the fill colour in force where the glyph is shown; after d0 the procedure sets its own colours. A glyph's own drawing never covers that glyph, nor is it the background A4 reads that glyph against.
type3Glyphs.inks: 1.6 (Codex v107 round 6): the inks A4 and A5 read for a Type 3 glyph. After d1, the fill colour and alpha in force where the glyph is shown, as for any glyph. After d0 the procedure paints in its OWN colours, so the glyph's ink is what the procedure paints: one colour and alpha shared by every paint operator in it is the ink; paints in several colours, of unread colour, soft-masked or in another blend mode, images or text inside the procedure leave the ink undecided (A4 REVIEW, text-colour-not-read); a procedure that paints nothing paints no ink (A5, like Tr 3). The caller's colour is never used for a d0 glyph.
type3Glyphs.notInspected: An implementation that cannot inspect a Type 3 glyph's drawing (it does not expand procedures, or a procedure cannot be read) MUST add checksSkipped {check:"A1", reason:"type3-glyph-not-inspected", page, count} and an A1 finding with verdict review and noteKey type3-not-inspected, and MUST NOT return pass for that file: the verdict is at least review.

candidate.$comment: A 'cover candidate' (黒塗り候補). Evaluated on the EFFECTIVE region: shape transformed by CTM and intersected with the current clip. A shading (requirements.shading) is a cover whose colour is unknown: never a dark candidate, always reported.

opaque.$comment: 1.7: a blend mode decides HOW a paint can hide what is under it. Normal and Compatible replace it: a dark paint is a cover (fail) and an opaque light one is nonDarkOpaqueCover (review). Multiply and Darken keep the darker of paint and backdrop, so they hide only by being dark: a dark one is a cover, a light one hides nothing and is no cover at all (a pale Multiply box over text is not an A1 review). Screen and Lighten mirror them: they keep the lighter, so a dark one hides nothing and a light one hides like nonDarkOpaqueCover (review). Light means luminance >= 1 - candidate.dark.maxLuminance; an image is light or dark by the same pixel fractions as candidate.image. Any other blend mode is not opaque.

size.$comment: Agreed: short side >= 3pt and long side >= 6pt, no area rule. A single masked digit at 8pt is about 5x8pt and must qualify. Thin rules (< 3pt) stay excluded; draw order removes header bands and table fills.

rectangularity.$comment: Oriented (minimum-area) bounding box, so rotated rectangles qualify. Measured per closed subpath (1.3); a nested subpath the fill rule leaves unpainted is a hole, not part of the outer's cover

strokedPath.$comment: marker-style blackouts drawn with a thick stroke; region = a ribbon per segment (1.3), closing segment included; never the area the path encloses. 1.6: built in user space (half the line width either side, caps by J, joins by j and M, a degenerate subpath only with round caps, a zero-length dash a dot with its cap shape) and transformed by the CTM; the width compared with minLineWidthPt is the width on the page across the segment, |det CTM| * w / |CTM * direction|

image.$comment: an image counts as a cover candidate over the area where >= 95% of its decoded pixels are dark. 1.6: its region is the parallelogram its matrix maps the unit square to (with the clip); locally, under a glyph, by cells (see cells). ImageMask: candidate when the fill colour is dark; for A6 its painted shape is read (changes 1.6). An image whose codec the implementation cannot decode is NOT a candidate; see imageDecoding.

cells.rule: 1.6: a glyph box is divided into perGlyphSide x perGlyphSide cells along and across the line; all of them are in the denominator. A cell is dark when at least minDarkPixelFraction of its samples that lie on the image and inside its effective region are at most darkPixelLuminance, and at least one does (a cell off the image is not dark; an unreadable pixel counts as dark). The glyph lies on the image's dark area when at least checks.A1.coverFail of its cells are dark.

image.sampling: 1.6: one sample per cell of a 64 x 64 grid over the region's bounding box (and samplesPerCellSide^2 per glyph cell), each at the fixed Halton offset of the cell's 1-based index (radical inverse base 2 across, base 3 down), never at the cell's midpoint (#185); only samples inside the region and on the image count

nonDarkOpaqueCover.$comment: An opaque NON-dark fill drawn over earlier text also hides it (white-box cover, grey redaction box). Reported as A1 review, not fail, to avoid failing Excel-style cell overflow.

weakCover.$comment: 1.7: a paint that would be a cover but for something this contract cannot measure - a soft mask (how much it lets through is per pixel; candidate.opaque.softMaskMeansNotOpaque keeps it from being a blackout), or a fill whose subpath crosses or touches itself (its loops may be exact, but rectangularity cannot rule a self-crossing outline out). It stays in the cover lists as a WEAK cover: text under it with coveredFraction >= coverFail is A1 review (detail text-under-weak-cover), invisible text under it is A5 review; never fail, never dropped (#236, #239, #240, #253).

glyphBox.rule: Horizontal writing: x from the glyph origin to origin + advance (Tw/Tc/Tz applied); y from baseline + descent to baseline + ascent with a FIXED ascent of 0.8 em and descent of -0.2 em; then transformed by Tm x CTM. Vertical writing: see vertical. Both implementations MUST use this box, not ink bounds, so coverage fractions agree.
glyphBox.unknownGlyph: A glyph never drops out of coverage because its character is unknown or unmappable; only a glyph that maps to white space may be ignored (1.5, #158).

vertical.appliesWhen: the font writes vertically: /WMode 1 in its CMap, or a predefined vertical CMap (a name ending in -V, e.g. Identity-V, UniJIS-UCS2-V)
vertical.rule: In text space at the glyph origin: across the line x0 = origin.x - halfWidthEm, x1 = origin.x + halfWidthEm (in em, times Tfs); along the line y1 = origin.y, y0 = origin.y - advance, where advance is the vertical displacement (1 em by the default /DW2, plus Tc and Tw); then transformed by Tm x CTM. The 0.8/-0.2 em pair does not apply.

glyphBox.$comment: FontDescriptor /Ascent and /Descent are deliberately NOT read: pdf.js and PDFium expose them differently and missing/zero values are common, so a fixed box is the only one both engines compute identically.
glyphBox.coverage: coveredFraction(glyphBox, covers) is the area of the glyph box inside the UNION of the covers' effective regions over the glyph box's area (1.4). For dark covers it is taken over every dark cover drawn after the glyph at once (for A3, the dark covers of the one annotation's appearance); a cover that is not dark is measured on its own

imageDecoding.rule: When an implementation cannot read an image's pixels (typically /DCTDecode, /JPXDecode, /JBIG2Decode or /CCITTFaxDecode, depending on the engine), every check that needs that image's pixels yields REVIEW for the affected region, never pass, and the report adds a checksSkipped entry with reason image-pixels-not-readable, the page, the count of such images, and detail = the terminal filter name when known.
imageDecoding.$comment: detail is the terminal filter name without the slash, e.g. DCTDecode (v1 put it in the reason as image-codec-not-decodable:<Filter>). v1.2: a filter name ISO 32000 does not define (Table 6, or an inline-image abbreviation of one, Table 92) is written as other, never the document's spelling; unreadable when the filter chain cannot be read. Such an image is also not a cover candidate (its darkness is unknown). Corpus cases whose verdict depends on this carry expect.acceptVerdicts.

checks.title: 不透明な図形・画像の下に取り出せるテキスト
checks.rule: glyph drawn before candidates with coveredFraction >= coverFail against the union of the dark candidates drawn after it (glyphBox.coverage, 1.4). An opaque non-dark cover gives review (candidate.nonDarkOpaqueCover); a cover of unreadable colour (requirements.shading) gives review with noteKey fill-colour-unreadable; an image whose pixels cannot be read gives review with checksSkipped image-pixels-not-readable (imageDecoding); unread content gives checksSkipped content-truncated; Type 3 glyphs not inspected give type3Glyphs.notInspected; an internal failure while examining a page gives checksSkipped check-failed and the page-not-examined finding (verdicts.reviewFloor).

checks.title: 黒塗りが文字に一部しかかかっていない
checks.rule: coverPartialMin <= coveredFraction < coverFail for a glyph drawn before dark candidates, coveredFraction taken against their union (glyphBox.coverage, 1.4)

checks.title: 未適用の /Redact、または注釈で隠している
checks.rule: Any /Redact annotation (regardless of what is under it). Otherwise an annotation appearance (requirements.annotationAppearance) that covers earlier text, graded by the ladder.

ladder.fail: /Redact; or an opaque DARK appearance (candidate.dark, any subtype, /Highlight included) covering text with coveredFraction >= coverPartialMin. Every cover of the annotation's appearance is considered (1.3): a dark one anywhere in it decides, even after a non-dark one drawn first
ladder.review: an opaque appearance that is NOT dark covering text with coveredFraction >= coverFail (nonDarkOpaqueCover applied to annotations)
ladder.none: a /Highlight whose appearance is not dark: a highlighter hides nothing

checks.title: 白文字・背景同色・ページ外・クリップ外の文字
checks.rule: text whose |L(text) - L(background)| < hiddenContrast, where background = colour painted at the glyph centre BEFORE the text (paper white when nothing): FAIL regardless of proximity. Glyph box outside the CropBox, or clipped out (1.6: less than coverPartialMin of the glyph box inside the union of the clip pieces, judged per glyph): FAIL when within nearCandidatePt of a candidate, else REVIEW. Tr 3 text is A5, not A4. 1.6: the text's inks are its fill for Tr 0/2/4/6 and its stroke for 1/2/5/6; it is the same as the background only when EVERY ink is; an ink of unread colour with no read ink standing out is REVIEW (text-colour-not-read). 1.6 (Codex v107 round 5): the background is the paint whose REALLY painted region (fill rule, holes, dash gaps, the clip's real region) contains the glyph centre - never a hull; only an over-statement known and the centre in it: REVIEW. Each ink counts with its alpha: alpha * |B(ink, bg) - bg| >= hiddenContrast shows (B the blend mode on luminance), so faint ink (0 < alpha) that adds less than hiddenContrast to its background is the same as the background, wherever it is; a soft-masked or otherwise-blended ink is REVIEW. Text that paints nothing (Tr 3/7, every ink at alpha 0) is A5's. Text clip modes Tr 4-7 clip at ET (changes 1.6).
checks.imageBackground: when the topmost painter under the glyph centre is an image, background = mean luminance of the image pixels under the glyph box; if its pixels cannot be read: REVIEW plus checksSkipped {check:"A4", reason:"image-pixels-not-readable", page, count, detail} (see imageDecoding), never pass
checks.clipVisibility: 1.6: per glyph, visible only when area(glyphBox inside the union of the clip pieces) / area(glyphBox) >= coverPartialMin. The pieces are the clip's real region (no hull of a concave subpath, no overlap the fill rule leaves out). The union MUST be computed, never a summed area; a bounded union that exceeds its bound computes exactly or floors the page at review (#160-#170).

checks.title: 黒塗りの下の不可視テキスト（Tr 3）
checks.rule: Tr 3 (or 7) glyph with coveredFraction >= coverPartialMin under a candidate (glyph box, not run origin) 1.6: in either draw order; under an image whose pixels cannot be read, or a cover of unread colour, REVIEW. 1.6 (the A4/A5 division): A5 is text that paints NOTHING - Tr 3, Tr 7, or every ink at an alpha of exactly 0 - judged like Tr 3. Faint ink (alpha above 0) paints something and is A4's.

checks.title: 画像の上に黒い図形を重ねただけ
checks.rule: image drawn, then a candidate over it, AND the decoded image pixels under the candidate are NOT dark (darkPixelFraction < candidate.image.minDarkPixelFraction).
